problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 8 & 6\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
- For the matrix $P$, we have

$$
det(P)=4\cdot 6-8\cdot 3=0.
$$

Because $det(P)=0,$ we conclude that $P$ is not invertible. Since $P$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $P$ is singular.

- For the matrix $Q$, we have

$$
det(Q)=1\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-1)=0.
$$

Because $det(Q)=0,$ we conclude that $Q$ is not invertible. Since $Q$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $Q$ is singular.

- The matrix $R$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

Therefore, only $P$ and $Q$ are singular.
